purpose: Test a synthetic semantic bridge between GitLab and Mattermost with idempotent ingestion, provenance and independent verification.

activities.label: deduplicate and order synthetic GitLab events
compile a provenance-bearing Mattermost representation and dry-run action
attack identity, provenance, permissions, freshness and claimed success

queries.expression: are duplicate and out-of-order deliveries normalized without changing entity identity
does every representation claim retain a qualified source reference
is an external effect verified against the source of truth rather than the target representation

assumptions: GitLab remains authoritative for the synthetic merge request and pipeline state.
An event ID is stable for idempotent delivery within the fixture.
A project-qualified entity reference is sufficient for this first bridge prototype.
The Mattermost action is low-risk but still requires explicit confirmation before any future write.
No network call or human data is necessary to test the contract boundary.
kill_tests: Missing source references block representation claims.
Missing Mattermost permission blocks the target action.
Claimed success without source observation blocks verification.
unknowns: Whether the contract remains sufficient for real OAuth, webhook signatures and token rotation.
How an institution declares mappings when the two applications expose different roles and permissions.
Whether a contextual map improves task completion compared with native GitLab and Mattermost views.
How to verify partial failure when a target message is delivered but the source changes concurrently.
Whether the same kernel transfers to OpenEMR and Nextcloud without domain-specific clinical assumptions.
